analysis: ESP32 UART RAM comparison: measured Roo endpoint versus lwIP configuration and object sizes
platform: Classic ESP32, Arduino-ESP32 3.3.7, ESP-IDF 87912cd291, Xtensa GCC 14.2.0
method: Compile the supplied source with the benchmark compiler arguments, replacing its input translation unit. Read BSS symbol sizes using native xtensa-esp-elf-nm -S --radix=d. No alternative firmware was linked, flashed or RAM-profiled.

assumptions: One new TCP socket over a new PPPoS interface; TCP/IP task is not already running.
Hold UART backend cost equal to the measured Roo driver plus Arduino event task solely to expose protocol differences; a real PPP integration can use a different task/ring architecture.
Both configured TCP send and receive capacities are occupied simultaneously. This is a bidirectional buffering model, not the one-way benchmark traffic profile or idle allocation.
excludes: Task control/runtime and allocator overhead for new lwIP allocations
Core and per-socket mailboxes, synchronization and socket/global bookkeeping
TCP/IP packet/segment headers and pbuf descriptors
Transient PPP input/output framing buffers and parser packet assembly
ESP-NETIF adapter/event-loop state and other enabled networking services

limits: This is not a measured total lwIP footprint or a throughput comparison.
TCP windows are capacities, not eagerly allocated payload arrays. Queued traffic drives dynamic heap use.
The installed SDK defaults differ from generic ESP-IDF Kconfig defaults; use the compiled values above.
PPP control state includes 4364 bytes of embedded optional VJ compression state. Removing that feature requires rebuilding the SDK, not just disabling negotiation at runtime.
Shared infrastructure may already be paid for by Wi-Fi/Ethernet. A tuned or already-running lwIP configuration can be more competitive than this new-stack model.
